summary: A heat pump can very likely heat this house, but whether the existing radiators are big enough is still open. The bill and the house size point to different heat loads, so the bill should be checked first.

thresholds.result: yellow: needs 55-60 C, higher running cost
needs > 60 C: some radiators should be upgraded

boundaries.how: Side photo of a typical radiator plus its height and width

reasons.text: Two-pipe system: all radiators get water at the same temperature.
The two heat-load estimates disagree (by area 5.0-7.5 kW, by bill 9.9-13.2 kW).

homeowner_can_provide: Does the bill cover a full year and all heated rooms, and is any other heat source used?
Current flow temperature setting of the boiler, if known
technician_checks: Outdoor unit placement, sound and permits
assumptions: Full-load hours 1800-2100 h (official approx. 2,000; range ours)
Hot-water share of the bill uncertain (unknown or solar thermal): subtract 0 to full per-person amount
Mixed system, heat share per circuit unknown: radiators assumed to carry the full load (conservative)
Radiator rating scaled by face area from 600 x 1000 mm (rough)
Radiator output vs temperature: EN 442, n = 1.3, 10 K spread
Heat pump also covers hot water, at the same JAZ as space heating
